verified_ballot_note: Third pass (Sept 17, 2026): verified against the Sumter County Supervisor of Elections' official 2026 General Election sample ballot, which lists Samantha Scott (REP) and Pamala Kaye Bivins (DEM) for State Representative, District 52, with no write-in line. Position research: Scott was seated March 25, 2026, after the regular session ended, so her only floor record is the June 2026 special session; her campaign site states values rather than issue positions, and no questionnaire responses were found. Bivins' site lists priorities without detailed positions. Sources: https://elections.sumtercountyfl.gov/DocumentCenter/View/332/2026-General-Sample-Ballot ; https://files.floridados.gov/media/710302/2026_nge_sum_english.pdf

candidates.name: Samantha Scott
candidates.photo_source: Florida House of Representatives member page (MemberId=5070); portrait image URL on that page not verified because the site was blocked in this sandbox
candidates.occupation: State Representative; director of marketing for Mike Scott Plumbing (family business); real estate professional; former executive director of the Sumter County Chamber of Commerce
candidates.background: Scott is a lifelong Sumter County resident from Bushnell, born June 18, 1981, in Orlando; she and her husband Shawn have five children and two grandchildren. She works as director of marketing for the family plumbing company and in real estate, and earlier served as executive director of the Sumter County Chamber of Commerce. She chaired the Sumter County Republican Executive Committee, chairs the Republican Party of Florida's Moms Coalition, was a 2024 Republican National Convention delegate, and was appointed by Gov. Ron DeSantis to the Lake-Sumter State College board of trustees in June 2025. After Rep. John Temple resigned Sept. 18, 2025, to become president of Lake-Sumter State College, Scott won the March 24, 2026 special election for District 52 without opposition after her only opponent withdrew, and was sworn in March 25, 2026, after the regular session had ended; she voted in the June 2026 special session on property taxes.
candidates.primary_result: No primary opponent; the Sumter County sample ballot lists her as the Republican nominee for Nov. 3, 2026.

taxes.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

property_tax.summary: On June 2, 2026, Scott voted yes on CS/HJR 1F, which placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; the measure passed the House 75-26. A vote to refer the amendment is treated here as leaning support; she has not published a statement on Amendment 3.

record.item: Legislative record context: the 2026 regular session ended March 13, 2026, before Scott assumed office on March 25, so she sponsored no regular-session bills. She was seated during the March 2026 special session and served during the April 28-May 1, 2026 special session (congressional redistricting, AI consumer protections, 'medical freedom') and the June 1-3, 2026 special session in which the House passed HJR 1-F, the homestead property-tax constitutional amendment now on the Nov. 3 ballot as Amendment 3, by 75-26. Her individual roll-call votes and any special-session bill sponsorships could not be retrieved in this sandbox (flhouse.gov, LobbyTools and her campaign news page were blocked).

candidates.name: Pamala Kaye Bivins
candidates.photo_source: Campaign website (og:image not verified; site blocked in this sandbox). Alternative: City of Wildwood commissioner page.
candidates.occupation: Former Wildwood city commissioner and mayor pro tem
candidates.background: Bivins (also known as Pamala Harrison-Bivins) was born and raised in Wildwood and is a lifetime resident. She served more than 25 years on the Wildwood City Commission, including as mayor pro tem, and resigned in November 2025 to run for the Florida House. She opened a campaign account for the HD 52 special election but withdrew before the qualifying deadline, leaving Samantha Scott unopposed; she then filed for the regular 2026 cycle as the Democratic candidate. Ballotpedia lists her as the Democratic candidate in the Aug. 18, 2026 primary advancing to the Nov. 3, 2026 general election.
candidates.primary_result: No primary opponent; the Sumter County sample ballot lists her as the Democratic nominee for Nov. 3, 2026.
